```{r}
# Cattle, pigs and sheep on farms in each of the four townships, from the
# Censuses of Agriculture of 2011, 2016 and 2021. One row per animal, township
# and year; `status` is Statistics Canada's quality symbol for the figure, and
# `animals` is missing where 02_clean_data.R blanked a figure this site never
# uses (E, F or x).
livestock <- read_csv(
  here("posts", "agriculture", "data", "livestock.csv"),
  col_types = cols(year = col_integer(), animals = col_double(), .default = col_character())
)
```

## First finding as a plain-language heading

<!-- One or two paragraphs, then one chart. -->

::: panel-tabset
### Cattle

```{r}
#| label: livestock-cattle
#| output: asis

# ---- Shared by every livestock chart in the post -------------------------

# Where each animal's figures come from, for the source lines
livestock_tables <- tribble(
  ~animal,  ~table_2021,     ~table_2011_2016,
  "Cattle", "32-10-0370-01", "32-10-0424-01",
  "Pigs",   "32-10-0372-01", "32-10-0426-01",
  "Sheep",  "32-10-0371-01", "32-10-0425-01"
)

# Why a figure is missing, by the Statistics Canada symbol it carried before
# 02_clean_data.R blanked it. E figures exist but are never used on this site.
missing_reason <- c(
  F = "too unreliable to publish",
  E = "flagged use with caution, so not used",
  x = "suppressed for confidentiality"
)

# The townships in alphabetical order from the top, the same in every tab so
# that switching tabs changes the numbers and nothing else. A horizontal
# chart draws the first level at the bottom, hence rev().
township_levels <- livestock |>
  distinct(district) |>
  arrange(desc(district)) |>
  pull(district)

# A note naming the figures Statistics Canada grades D, "acceptable": the
# weakest grade it publishes without a caution flag (style rule 9c). NULL when
# the chart has none, which cwr_caption() treats as no note.
grade_note <- function(d) {
  graded <- d |>
    filter(status == "D") |>
    mutate(entry = paste0(cwr_short_name(district), " (", year, ")")) |>
    pull(entry)
  if (length(graded) == 0) return(NULL)
  paste0("Graded acceptable quality by Statistics Canada: ", str_flatten_comma(graded, ", and "))
}

# ---- 2021 bar chart for one animal ---------------------------------------
livestock_bars <- function(which_animal) {
  bar_data <- livestock |>
    filter(animal == which_animal, year == 2021) |>
    mutate(
      district = factor(district, levels = township_levels),
      # A missing figure is named on its empty row instead of a number
      label = if_else(
        is.na(animals),
        str_to_sentence(missing_reason[status]),
        label_comma(accuracy = 1)(animals)
      ),
      # Whether a number fits inside its bar, the same test as the welcome
      # post's bar charts: the axis runs to about 1.2 times the longest bar,
      # and roughly 45 characters of label fit across it on a phone
      inside = !is.na(animals) &
        animals >= (str_length(label) + 1.5) * (max(animals, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.2 / 45),
      # Missing rows put their text at the baseline, never a zero-length bar,
      # just right of it. hjust is a fraction of the text's own width, so a
      # fixed nudge rather than a negative hjust lines every such row up.
      label_x = coalesce(animals, max(animals, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.015),
      label_hjust = case_when(inside ~ 1.15, is.na(animals) ~ 0, .default = -0.15),
      label_colour = case_when(inside ~ "white", is.na(animals) ~ "grey30", .default = "black")
    )

  ggplot(bar_data, aes(y = district)) +
    geom_col(
      data = bar_data |> filter(!is.na(animals)),
      aes(x = animals),
      fill = dodgerblue,
      width = 0.7
    ) +
    # The baseline, as a segment that stops just past the bars rather than a
    # line the full height of the panel
    annotate(
      "segment",
      x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0.5, yend = length(township_levels) + 0.5,
      colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = label_x, label = label, hjust = label_hjust, colour = label_colour),
      size = label_size * 0.8
    ) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    # drop = FALSE keeps a township's row even when it has no bar;
    # cwr_short_name() writes North Dumfries as "N. Dumfries" (style rule 2b)
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE, labels = cwr_short_name) +
    # Room on the right for a number that sits outside its bar
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20))) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    # Every bar carries its number, so the value axis and its gridlines go
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )
}

livestock_bars_caption <- function(which_animal) {
  table_2021 <- livestock_tables |>
    filter(animal == which_animal) |>
    pull(table_2021)
  cwr_caption(
    paste("Statistics Canada Table", table_2021),
    notes = grade_note(livestock |> filter(animal == which_animal, year == 2021))
  )
}

# Alt text built from the plotted figures
livestock_bars_alt <- function(which_animal) {
  entries <- livestock |>
    filter(animal == which_animal, year == 2021) |>
    arrange(district) |>
    mutate(entry = if_else(
      is.na(animals),
      paste0(district, " no figure, ", missing_reason[status]),
      paste0(district, " ", label_comma(accuracy = 1)(animals))
    )) |>
    pull(entry)
  paste0(
    "Horizontal bars for the four townships showing ", str_to_lower(which_animal),
    " on farms on census day, 11 May 2021: ", paste(entries, collapse = "; "), "."
  )
}

p <- livestock_bars("Cattle") +
  labs(
    title = "Cattle on farms in the four townships, 2021",   # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when",
    caption = livestock_bars_caption("Cattle")
  )

cwr_figure(p, "fig-livestock-cattle", alt = livestock_bars_alt("Cattle"))
```

### Cattle

```{r}
#| label: livestock-years-cattle
#| output: asis

# ---- Dot plot of 2011, 2016 and 2021 for one animal ----------------------
# One row per township, one dot per census, joined by a grey line from the
# lowest count to the highest so the spread reads at a glance. The ggdumbbell
# template with a third dot; a slope chart or small line charts were the
# alternatives, but with only three censuses and four townships the dots put
# every figure on one row.
year_colours <- c("2011" = habsred, "2016" = cowboysilver, "2021" = dodgerblue)

livestock_dots <- function(which_animal) {
  dot_data <- livestock |>
    filter(animal == which_animal) |>
    mutate(
      district = factor(district, levels = township_levels),
      year = factor(year)
    ) |>
    # Drawn in year order, so where two dots overlap the 2021 one is on top
    arrange(year)

  # The grey line behind each row's dots, from its lowest to highest count.
  # Missing figures are left out, so the line never bridges a gap.
  spans <- dot_data |>
    filter(!is.na(animals)) |>
    summarise(low = min(animals), high = max(animals), .by = district)

  ggplot(dot_data, aes(y = district)) +
    geom_segment(
      data = spans,
      aes(x = low, xend = high, yend = district),
      colour = "grey70",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    # A missing figure gets no dot; na.rm = TRUE drops it without a warning
    geom_point(aes(x = animals, colour = year), size = 4, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = year_colours, name = NULL) +
    # Thousands on the axis (style rule 1c): three-digit labels fit on a
    # phone, and the subtitle says the scale. The axis starts at zero so a
    # row's position is its size, not just its rank.
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, big.mark = ","),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
      position = "top"
    ) +
    expand_limits(x = 0) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE, labels = cwr_short_name) +
    theme(
      # Horizontal chart: gridlines run vertically
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      # The year key on its own row under the subtitle, keys under the
      # title's left edge
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification.top = "left",
      legend.location = "plot",
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    )
}

# Notes: what is missing and why, any figure graded acceptable, and
# Statistics Canada's caution on comparing one census with another (its
# footnotes on all six tables).
livestock_dots_caption <- function(which_animal) {
  animal_data <- livestock |> filter(animal == which_animal)

  missing <- animal_data |>
    filter(is.na(animals)) |>
    summarise(
      places = str_flatten_comma(cwr_short_name(district), " and "),
      .by = c(year, status)
    ) |>
    mutate(entry = paste0(places, " ", year, " (", missing_reason[status], ")")) |>
    pull(entry)

  tables <- livestock_tables |>
    filter(animal == which_animal) |>
    select(table_2011_2016, table_2021) |>
    unlist(use.names = FALSE)

  cwr_caption(
    c(paste("Statistics Canada Tables", tables[1]), tables[-1]),
    notes = c(
      if (length(missing) > 0) paste0("Not shown: ", paste(missing, collapse = "; ")),
      grade_note(animal_data),
      "Statistics Canada advises caution comparing censuses: farm definitions and locations changed"
    )
  )
}

livestock_dots_alt <- function(which_animal) {
  entries <- livestock |>
    filter(animal == which_animal) |>
    arrange(district, year) |>
    mutate(entry = if_else(
      is.na(animals),
      paste0("no figure in ", year, " (", missing_reason[status], ")"),
      paste0(label_comma(accuracy = 1)(animals), " in ", year)
    )) |>
    summarise(entry = paste(entry, collapse = ", "), .by = district) |>
    mutate(entry = paste0(district, ": ", entry)) |>
    pull(entry)
  paste0(
    "Dot plot of ", str_to_lower(which_animal), " on farms in each of the four townships ",
    "at the Censuses of Agriculture of 2011 (red dot), 2016 (grey) and 2021 (blue). ",
    paste(entries, collapse = ". "), "."
  )
}

p <- livestock_dots("Cattle") +
  labs(
    title = "Cattle on farms in the four townships, 2011 to 2021",   # working title, descriptive only
    subtitle = "Subtitle: what is measured, for whom, and when",
    caption = livestock_dots_caption("Cattle")
  )

cwr_figure(p, "fig-livestock-years-cattle", alt = livestock_dots_alt("Cattle"))
```
